title: Perfect projection formula for reductions
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be schemes, $f:X\to Y$ a morphism, and $(A,I)$ the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $A$ commutative Noetherian, $P_n=A/I^n$ finite as a set and perfect in $D(A)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ and use the ordinary, uncompleted derived categories of $A_T$-module sheaves. The coefficient identification $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ is the canonical one of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]; use the operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and their K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Fix $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The full isomorphism locus of the map $\pi_{f,K,P}$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map], for $P\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, is a thick triangulated subcategory containing every finite free coefficient sheaf $A_Y^{\oplus m}$. It contains every site-perfect complex [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]: here site-perfect means locally on the site isomorphic to a bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free coefficient sheaves, with bounds allowed to depend on the covering object. For every $n\geq1$ the canonical pullback comparison $Lf^*(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$ identifies the projection map with an isomorphism
$$\pi_n:(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{A_Y}(P_n)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K_n,\qquad K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_X}(P_n)_X.$$
Its inverse $\rho_n$ agrees with the signed-totalization inverse for a finite-projective resolution of $P_n$. These maps and inverses are independent of the chosen resolution and commute with quotient tower maps, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base change in the projection-formula square of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-base-change-naturality]. For proper $f$, they also agree with the identity-compactification formula [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-identity-compactification].

proof.text: The profinite comparison supplies $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ compatibly with quotient projections. Thus the operations and projection definitions use the ordinary ringed mate. For $F(P)=Rf_*K\otimes^LP$ and $G(P)=Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*P)$, its shift equation identifies the isomorphism locus with the all-shifts locus. Apply the shift-saturated locus theorem: it is thick triangulated.

The mate lemma gives $\pi_{A_Y}=1$. Additivity and naturality with finite-biproduct injections and projections make $\pi_{A_Y^{\oplus m}}$ the diagonal matrix of identities; it is invertible also for $m=0$. These statements apply on localized ringed topoi as well.

proof.text: Choose local bounded models for a site-perfect $P$. The restriction lemma identifies the restricted mates. Their terms are finite-free retracts, hence belong to the local thick loci of steps 1–2. Bounded-complex devissage puts each model there. Local detection then gives invertibility at $P$; bounds need not be uniform.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula, locality and stupid truncations

proof.text: For $P_n$, the perfect-ring definition and completed-constant reduction give a bounded finite-free-retract $A_T$-model of $(P_n)_T$. Step 3 applies. The equation $\pi_{X,n}c_f=c_{f,n}f^{-1}\pi_{Y,n}$ makes $c_{f,n}$ coefficient-linear; the operations have exact identified-coefficient pullback. Thus $Lf^*(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$.

Compute the counit projection mate on mixed K-flat representatives by lem-weil-pbc-proetale-mixed-projection-mate. Naturality in K and the coefficient transports its equation along the chosen K-injective model, the quotient representative, and the canonical quotient pullback comparison. This identifies the forward reduction map with localization of the signed total mate. tensorAdjunctionTotal_isIso, using ordinaryUnit_coherence and the bounded degreewise finite-free retract package, proves its inverse identity. Uniqueness of inverses then identifies the specified total inverse with rho_n, independently of the chosen model or splittings.

source.place: Second paragraph and third paragraph: signed totalization and uniqueness

proof.text: Mate naturality gives quotient and operator squares; profinite comparison identifies the pulled-back quotient maps. The base-change lemma supplies the forward exchange square. The new pullback-model lemma makes $Lg^*$ of the model in step 4 strict-perfect, with its mapped splittings. Totalization inverts its lower projection arrow. For base change the upper arrow is $Lg^*\pi_n$, whose inverse is $Lg^*\rho_n$ because functors preserve inverse equations. For any forward square $b\pi=\pi\prime a$ with $\rho,\rho\prime$ inverse to $\pi,\pi\prime$, $\rho\prime b=\rho\prime b\pi\rho=\rho\prime\pi\prime a\rho=a\rho$. This gives every inverse square, without inverting exchange.
For proper $f$, the identity-compactification lemma identifies its arrows with these $\pi$ and $\rho$. Apply it to the model of step 4; step 5 identifies them with $\pi_n$ and $\rho_n$.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every $n$ there is a natural isomorphism

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n
\xrightarrow[\pi_n]{\sim}Rf_*K_n
$$

whose inverse is $\rho_n$. The families $(\pi_n)$ and $(\rho_n)$ commute
with the reduction tower, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base
change.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Choose a strict-perfect package $F_n^\bullet\to P_n$. Signed totalization
gives inverse arrows

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LF_n^\bullet
\mathrel{\substack{\xrightarrow{\ \pi_n\ }\\[-2pt]
\xleftarrow[\ \rho_n\ ]{}}}
Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*F_n^\bullet).
$$

Because $P_n$ is constant, $Lf^*P_n=P_n$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$.
The identity-compactification lemma shows that this is also the open/proper
compactification composite for proper $f$. The totalization lemma gives
$\rho_n\pi_n=1$ and $\pi_n\rho_n=1$. Uniqueness of an inverse makes the map
independent of the strict-perfect package. Tower, operator, and base-change
compatibility are exactly the preceding two lemmas. This expands the
finite-projective argument located at Tag `0944`.

blueprint_update.statement:
For fixed $f$ and $K$, the full subcategory of objects $P$ for which
$\pi_{f,K,P}$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] is an isomorphism is a
thick triangulated subcategory containing every finite free $A$-module. In
particular, it contains every perfect complex, and for every $n$ there is a
natural isomorphism

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n
\xrightarrow[\pi_n]{\sim}Rf_*K_n
$$

whose inverse is $\rho_n$. The families $(\pi_n)$ and $(\rho_n)$ commute
with the reduction tower, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base
change.

proof.text:
For $P=A$ the map $\pi_{f,K,A}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] is the canonical tensor identity, an
isomorphism; for a finite free $P=A^m$ it is the direct sum of finitely many
of these, so every finite free $A$-module lies in the full subcategory. The
subcategory is triangulated-thick: it is closed under shifts ($Lf^*$, $Rf_*$
and tensor are exact triangulated by
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and commute with the shift comparisons),
under cones (applying $u:P_1\to P_2$ to the projection-formula maps makes the
cones of the $\pi$'s fit into a distinguished triangle, and the
two-out-of-three property gives the claim), and under direct summands (an
idempotent splitting of $P$ gives one of the isomorphism). Hence it contains
every perfect complex, i.e. every object of the thick triangulated
subcategory generated by the finite free modules, and in particular every
$P_n$'s finite free resolution in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], giving the displayed isomorphism
$(Rf_*K)\otimes_A^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K_n$.

Choose a strict-perfect package $F_n^\bullet\to P_n$. Signed totalization
gives inverse arrows

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LF_n^\bullet
\mathrel{\substack{\xrightarrow{\ \pi_n\ }\\[-2pt]
\xleftarrow[\ \rho_n\ ]{}}}
Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*F_n^\bullet).
$$

Because $P_n$ is constant, $Lf^*P_n=P_n$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$.
The identity-compactification lemma shows that this is also the open/proper
compactification composite for proper $f$. The totalization lemma gives
$\rho_n\pi_n=1$ and $\pi_n\rho_n=1$. Uniqueness of an inverse makes the map
independent of the strict-perfect package. Tower, operator, and base-change
compatibility are exactly the preceding two lemmas. This expands the
finite-projective argument located at Tag `0944`.
